chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, that a man was in Hamadan

he mentioned that his father died and he did not know this matter, so he bequeathed a bequest at the time of death and bequeathed that something be given in the Way of Allah, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about it, how should it be dealt with
so we informed him that he did not know this matter, so he said: 'If a man had bequeathed to me that I should place it with a Jew or a Christian, I would have placed it with them'
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin of it is only upon those who alter it'
So look to the one who goes out to this direction, meaning one of the borders/frontiers, so send it to him.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: Way of Allah (often referring to Jihad or charitable causes)
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرَ: This matter (referring to Wilayah or specific religious authority/knowledge)

ai.seo_question: How is a bequest for 'the Way of Allah' distributed if the specific recipient is unknown or if flexibility is allowed?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the principle of *tawassu'* (flexibility) in bequests, ruling that 'in the Way of Allah' is a broad category that can include non-Muslims, such as Jews or Christians, if the general purpose is fulfilled. He cites Quran 2:181 to demonstrate that altering the specific recipient does not invalidate the bequest, provided the core intent is maintained. This ruling is practically applied by directing the funds to a specific individual heading to the *thughur* (frontier borders) for jihad, highlighting the dynamic link between charitable bequests and communal defense in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Waleed, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub that,

‘A man was at Hamdaan mentioned that his father died and he did not recognise this matter (Al-Wilayah), so he bequeathed with a bequest during the death, and bequeathed that something be given in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> (Jihad). So he asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> how he should deal with it. So he informed him<sup>asws</sup> he did not recognise this matter (Al Wilayah)’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Even if a man had bequeathed to me that I<sup>asws</sup> should place it among the Jews or the Christians, I<sup>asws</sup> would have placed among these two.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [2:181] So the one who alters it after he has heard it, the sin of it then is only upon the one who alters it.
Therefore, look at the one who has gone out to these direction, meaning one of the borders, so send it to him’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has narrated the following: “A man of Hamadan

has said that his father died but he did not know this fact (the Divine Authority of A’immah). He made a will when he was about to die to give something in the way of Allah. He (the man from Hamadan) asked abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about it and that he did not know this fact (the Divine Authority of A’immah).
He (the Imam) said, ‘If the man had appointed me to execute his will to give to a Jews or Christians, I would have given it to them
because Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, “Whoever intentionally changes the will of a deceased person, he has committed a sin. Allah is All-hearing and All-knowing.” [2:181]
You must see who serves as guards and defenders of the borders; and give it to them.’”
